_comment: PERFORMANCE suite: the ingestion throughput of the mysqlcdc stream source -- the rows a stream publisher writes to its files per second, before a trigger makes them a manifest -- over 1000000 rows (250000 in each of the employeescdc tables accounts, ledger, devices, readings), loaded before the stream starts so it reads a backlog. The publisher (functions/perf_mysqlcdc.py::mysqlcdc_changes) is registered from the head: the 1000000 are changes it reads from the binlog, a replica with a server_id of its own; the head is the oldest binlog the server keeps, so what earlier runs on the container left is read and skipped too, and counts in the time. STAGES: (1) domains -- create the mysqlcdc domain, install employeescdc, create-data --size 2500; (2) collections, then a 60s pause so the source has captured the load before the stream starts; (3) functions -- register the publisher, which STARTS it; (4) actions -- scripts/cdc_throughput.py reads the stream worker's log until its files hold 1000000 rows or 10m has passed, and says in the step's note the end-to-end figure -- rows, files, MB, seconds from the plugin's run() to the last file, rows/s -- and the read figure -- rows the source yielded, the seconds the plugin waited on it for them, rows/s (PARTIAL when short; the step still passes); (5) monitor. Generated by gen_suites.py. Run one at a time -- lanes side by side share the machine and skew the figure: `tdd xp one-shot --suite performance/mysqlcdc_changes`.
